package_info.why_malicious: The package is not intentionally malicious, but contains a vulnerability (CVE-2020-7599) that causes sensitive pre-signed AWS S3 upload URLs to be logged at info or lower log levels. If these logs are exposed (such as in public CI/CD systems), attackers can obtain the URLs and use them to overwrite recently uploaded plugins with malicious artifacts, leading to potential supply chain compromise.

execution_context.file_location: Gradle build log output (when run with --info or lower log level)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Publishing plugin to AWS S3 using pre-signed URL: https://s3.amazonaws.com/gradle-plugins/....?AWSAccessKeyId=...&Expires=...&Signature=...
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During plugin publishing, the plugin logs a sensitive pre-signed AWS S3 upload URL to the build log at info or lower log levels, exposing the URL to anyone with access to the logs, which can enable unauthorized overwriting of the uploaded plugin.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Logging sensitive pre-signed AWS S3 upload URLs exposes credentials that can be used to overwrite published plugins. If logs are accessible to unauthorized parties, this creates a window for attackers to hijack the plugin distribution process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure build systems should never log sensitive credentials or pre-signed URLs at info or lower log levels. Such information should be redacted or only available at debug levels in secure environments. The actual behavior leaks a credential that can be used for unauthorized artifact overwrites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Logging pre-signed URLs for debugging purposes in a secure, private environment with restricted log access.
key_indicators: Presence of full pre-signed AWS S3 URLs in build logs
Logging occurs at info or lower log levels during plugin publishing
Potential for artifact overwrite using the exposed URL within its validity window

attack_chain.action: Plugin author publishes a plugin using the vulnerable com.gradle.plugin-publish plugin; a pre-signed AWS S3 URL is generated and logged at info or lower log level.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive pre-signed URL is exposed in build logs.

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers the exposed pre-signed URL in public or accessible CI build logs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the S3 upload endpoint for the plugin artifact.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the pre-signed URL to overwrite the recently uploaded plugin with a malicious artifact within the URL's validity window.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious plugin is distributed to users via the official plugin repository.

behavioral_signatures: Logging of pre-signed AWS S3 URLs containing 'AWSAccessKeyId' and 'Signature' parameters during plugin publishing
Exposure of sensitive credential-bearing URLs in build logs at info or lower log levels
Unusual S3 artifact overwrites occurring shortly after initial plugin upload
file_indicators: Gradle build logs containing full S3 pre-signed URLs with 'AWSAccessKeyId' and 'Signature' parameters
Log entries matching the pattern: 'Publishing plugin to AWS S3 using pre-signed URL:'
network_indicators: S3 PUT requests using pre-signed URLs found in build logs
Unexpected S3 PUT or POST requests to plugin artifact locations shortly after plugin publication
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Gradle build logs for the presence of pre-signed AWS S3 URLs, specifically those containing 'AWSAccessKeyId' and 'Signature' parameters, especially at info or lower log levels. Set up alerts for any log entries matching the pattern 'Publishing plugin to AWS S3 using pre-signed URL:'. Correlate with S3 access logs to detect unexpected PUT or POST requests to plugin artifact locations within the validity window of the pre-signed URL, and flag any artifact overwrites that occur shortly after plugin publication.
